sentences.en: PHIL: That lecture from the visiting speaker yesterday was good, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: PHIL: 昨天那位来访演讲者的讲座很不错，对吧？

sentences.en: LUCY: Yeah
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是啊。

sentences.en: I learned a lot from her about ocean biodiversity
sentences.zh: 我从她那里学到了很多关于海洋生物多样性的知识。

sentences.en: I've already done some reading on it, and I did an assignment on some of the problems associated with it last year, but I especially liked the way her lecture focused on more long-term issues
sentences.zh: 我之前已经就此做过一些阅读，而且去年还完成过一份关于相关问题的作业，但我尤其喜欢她讲座中聚焦于更长期议题的方式。

sentences.en: PHIL: Yes, things that aren't currently receiving widespread attention but are likely to be important in the future
sentences.zh: PHIL: 没错，就是那些目前尚未受到广泛关注、但未来很可能变得十分重要的问题。

sentences.en: That impressed me too
sentences.zh: 这一点也给我留下了深刻印象。

sentences.en: It wasn't exactly a feel-good conclusion because it's hard to see any real solution for a lot of the problems
sentences.zh: 不过，那并非一个令人安心的结论，因为许多问题似乎根本看不到切实可行的解决方案。

sentences.en: LUCY: No, though she did point to where policy changes could be made to protect our marine and coastal environments
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是的，尽管她确实指出了可在哪些方面调整政策，以保护我们的海洋与沿海环境。

sentences.en: PHIL: Mm
sentences.zh: PHIL: 嗯。

sentences.en: But that's just at a national level
sentences.zh: 但那仅限于国家层面。

sentences.en: The examples she gave were at a more global level, and they really made it clear to me just how wide-ranging the threats to ocean biodiversity are
sentences.zh: 她所举的例子则处于更广泛的全球层面，这让我真切意识到海洋生物多样性所面临的威胁范围之广。

sentences.en: LUCY: Yes, me too
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是的，我也有同感。

sentences.en: PHIL: The research project she described was impressive, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: PHIL: 她所描述的这项研究项目令人印象深刻，不是吗？

sentences.en: I'd have thought it was quite unusual to have so many experts working together
sentences.zh: 我原以为，能有如此多专家共同协作，实属罕见。

sentences.en: LUCY: Yeah, and from such different backgrounds
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是啊，而且他们来自如此迥异的背景。

sentences.en: Must have been a really exciting team to work with
sentences.zh: 想必那支团队合作起来一定非常令人振奋。

sentences.en: I'd heard of a couple of them before – they were involved in research way back in 2009 warning about the dangers of ocean pollution
sentences.zh: 我之前就听说过其中几位——早在2009年，他们就参与了有关海洋污染危害的预警研究。

sentences.en: PHIL: But now people are much more aware of that, aren't they?
sentences.zh: PHIL: 但如今人们对这个问题的关注度已高得多，不是吗？

sentences.en: LUCY: I suppose so
sentences.zh: LUCY: 我想是这样。

sentences.en: PHIL: Another thing about the research is that the team members came from all round the world
sentences.zh: PHIL: 这项研究的另一特点是，团队成员来自世界各地。

sentences.en: Though I suppose that's not unusual nowadays, now everyone can work remotely
sentences.zh: 虽然我想，如今这已不足为奇，毕竟现在人人都可以远程办公。

sentences.en: LUCY: Right
sentences.zh: LUCY: 好的。

sentences.en: I liked the way she didn't bombard us with figures – I mean, they were available, but she focused more on the general points they indicated
sentences.zh: 我喜欢她没有用大量数据轰炸我们——我的意思是，那些数据确实可供查阅，但她更侧重于阐述这些数据所体现的总体要点。

sentences.en: PHIL: Mm
sentences.zh: PHIL: 嗯。

sentences.en: And the description of improvements in systems used for tracking marine animals and things like robots were really interesting
sentences.zh: 关于追踪海洋动物的系统改进以及机器人等技术的介绍，真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: LUCY: Yes, and her description of how robotics can be used to investigate threats to biodiversity
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是的，还有她对如何利用机器人技术调查生物多样性威胁的描述。

sentences.en: PHIL: Absolutely
sentences.zh: PHIL: 没错。

sentences.en: PHIL: While you're here, can we talk about the list of resources we have to evaluate for the seminar tomorrow
sentences.zh: PHIL: 既然你在这儿，我们能聊聊明天研讨会需要评估的资源清单吗？

sentences.en: I've had a look at them all, but it's been a bit of a rush
sentences.zh: 我已通读了全部资料，但时间有点仓促。

sentences.en: LUCY: Yeah
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是啊。

sentences.en: What did you think of that article on invasive lionfish?
sentences.zh: 你觉得那篇关于入侵性狮子鱼的文章怎么样？

sentences.en: The one claiming they were expanding their habitat throughout the Mediterranean Sea
sentences.zh: 就是那篇声称它们正将栖息地扩展至整个地中海海域的文章。

sentences.en: PHIL: Well, the writer went on about how dangerous they were in environmental terms, which is probably true, but he didn't really provide much information to explain why
sentences.zh: PHIL: 嗯，作者大谈特谈它们在环境方面的危害性，这或许属实，但他并未提供太多信息来解释原因。

sentences.en: LUCY: I know what you mean
sentences.zh: LUCY: 我明白你的意思。

sentences.en: PHIL: I watched the documentary on microplastics, at least I started to, but then I found it was made ten years ago so I gave up
sentences.zh: PHIL: 我看了关于微塑料的纪录片，至少一开始看了，但后来发现它竟是十年前制作的，于是就放弃了。

sentences.en: LUCY: I watched to the end but you're right, it was showing its age
sentences.zh: LUCY: 我看完了，不过你说得对，片子确实显得过时了。

sentences.en: People had hardly heard of microplastics then, whereas now everyone knows about them and how dangerous they are
sentences.zh: 当时人们几乎还没听说过微塑料，而如今人人都知道它们及其危害性。

sentences.en: PHIL: Yeah
sentences.zh: PHIL: 是啊。

sentences.en: Did you listen to the podcast on ocean pollution?
sentences.zh: 你听了那期关于海洋污染的播客了吗？

sentences.en: LUCY: Mm
sentences.zh: LUCY: 嗯。

sentences.en: I didn't get anything out of it though
sentences.zh: 不过，我从中什么也没学到。

sentences.en: Most of it was stating the obvious
sentences.zh: 大部分内容都是在陈述显而易见的事实。

sentences.en: PHIL: Yes, it mentioned pesticides and plastic and things, and it clearly made the point that they were a bad thing, but everybody knows that anyway
sentences.zh: PHIL: 是的，它提到了杀虫剂和塑料之类的东西，并明确指出它们是有害的，但这一点大家本来就知道。

sentences.en: Did you read that book on coastal ecosystems?
sentences.zh: 你读过那本关于海岸生态系统的书吗？

sentences.en: LUCY: The one by John Harper?
sentences.zh: LUCY: 就是约翰·哈珀写的那本？

sentences.en: Yes, I found it hard going at first, it went into a lot of detail about things like the effects of offshore windfarms and fish farms, but actually I ended up with a much better understanding of the issues
sentences.zh: 是的，一开始我觉得读起来很吃力，书中详细探讨了近海风电场和水产养殖场的影响等问题，但最终我对相关议题的理解确实大大加深了。

sentences.en: PHIL: Yes, I agree and I thought it was a well-written summary of those
sentences.zh: PHIL: 是的，我同意，而且我认为这本书对这些议题的总结写得相当好。

sentences.en: And the diagrams helped a lot too
sentences.zh: 而且图示也帮了大忙。

sentences.en: LUCY: The article on metal toxicity was way above my head, I didn't know anything about how metals from industrial emissions react in the ocean... and I still don't understand it
sentences.zh: LUCY: 关于金属毒性的那篇文章完全超出了我的理解范围，我对工业排放的金属在海洋中如何发生反应一无所知……现在还是不懂。

sentences.en: PHIL: I gave up reading after the first chapter – I just couldn't follow it
sentences.zh: PHIL: 我读完第一章就放弃了——根本跟不上内容。

sentences.en: LUCY: That podcast on floating marine cities was interesting, though it presented a rather one-sided picture, I thought
sentences.zh: LUCY: 不过，那个关于漂浮海上城市的播客倒挺有意思，尽管我觉得它呈现的画面有些片面。

sentences.en: PHIL: Yes, it focused on how this would benefit people and ignored the effects on the environment
sentences.zh: PHIL: 是的，它只聚焦于这种城市将如何造福人类，却忽略了其对环境造成的影响。

sentences.en: LUCY: But anyway, shall we
sentences.zh: LUCY: 但不管怎样，我们是不是该……
